summary:
FSD (Supervised) is now a subscription product in the U.S.: Tesla's support page lists $99 a month and says it cannot be bought outright [2], after the one-time purchase was dropped in February 2026 [3]. Tesla reported 1.74 million active FSD subscriptions at the end of Q3, a count that includes earlier lifetime purchases, and says more than 75% of new North American deliveries in the quarter included FSD [4].

This week's software is update 2026.38.5.10, released October 20: FSD v14.3.13 for AI4 (HW4) cars and a new "v14.3 Lite" that brings parking, unparking and reversing to HW3 cars [1]. HW3 owners have still been told their computers will not run unsupervised FSD, with no clear upgrade plan [5]. On the Q3 call Tesla targeted Q2 2027 for unsupervised FSD in customer cars, starting with owners adding cars to its Robotaxi fleet inside Robotaxi zones [5][6]. AI5 has entered trial production but is not in customer cars [6].

Robotaxi runs without anyone on board in six metros (Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa) and with a safety driver in the Bay Area; Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville and San Antonio are listed as coming soon [7][8]. Tesla's new safety site claims 3.1 million autonomous miles through October 18 with no reported injuries; that is company data [8].

In Europe the product is now called Tesla Assisted Driving; nine countries have approved it and an EU-wide vote is expected in December [6][11]. In California, police said a Tesla driver told them FSD was engaged when the car struck and killed a 71-year-old pedestrian on Interstate 80 on October 23; it is not established whether the driver or the software braked and steered [10].

price.purchase: Can't be bought outright: Tesla says FSD (Supervised) is subscription-only [2]. The $8,000 one-time purchase ended after February 14, 2026 [3].
price.note: FSD bought outright by an earlier owner stays with the car unless it was transferred away before March 31, 2026; a previous owner's subscription does not carry over, and Luxe Package FSD may carry over depending on when it was bought [2].

versions.note: Released October 20; MLIR compiler rewrite, better emergency-vehicle, school-bus and traffic-light handling, unified model with Robotaxi and Smart Summon [1].
Distilled from v14 for HW3: adds parking, unparking, reversing and Arrival Options [1].

hardware.note: HW2 went into S and X from October 2016 to about August 2017; S/X built earlier in 2016 have the older Autopilot 1 hardware and no FSD path [13].

hardware.fsd: None as built; runs FSD (Supervised) only if the computer was retrofitted to HW3, which Tesla did free for owners who had bought FSD [13].
hardware.note: HW2.5 from about August 2017 to March 2019; 2017 is a split year with HW2. Check the Autopilot computer line in Additional Vehicle Information [12][13].

hardware.note: HW3 from March 22, 2019 [13]; 2019 is a split year with HW2.5 and 2023 a split year with AI4 (cars bought after March 2023 likely AI4) [12].

check: In the car: Controls > Software > Additional Vehicle Information shows the Autopilot computer (2.5, 3 or 4); this needs software 2024.38 or later [12].
Controls > Software also shows whether Full Self-Driving Capability is in the car's included package [2].
Front cameras: AI4 cars show two red lenses and one black dummy lens; AI4 side repeaters have a red tint [12].
Build date: S/X after about March 2023, U.S. Model Y after late May 2023 and the 2024 Model 3 are likely AI4 [12].
transfer: You can no longer move FSD to another car or account: Tesla's FSD (Supervised) Transfer Program ended on March 31, 2026 [2][3]. If you sell a car whose FSD was bought outright, the purchase stays with that car, so the next owner gets it [2]. If you had a subscription, it ends with your ownership and the buyer must subscribe on their own Tesla account [2]. Owners who bought FSD before the change keep it on the car permanently, but a new Tesla means a new $99 subscription [3]. We found no current transfer offer; the Tesla app 4.62 adds FSD referral rewards, which are not a transfer [18].

pt.summary:
O FSD (Supervised) agora é vendido só por assinatura nos EUA: a página de suporte da Tesla indica US$ 99 por mês e diz que não é possível comprá-lo à vista [2]; a compra única acabou em fevereiro de 2026 [3]. A Tesla informou 1,74 milhão de assinaturas ativas no fim do 3º trimestre, número que inclui compras vitalícias antigas, e diz que mais de 75% das entregas novas na América do Norte incluíram FSD [4].

O software desta semana é a atualização 2026.38.5.10, de 20 de outubro: FSD v14.3.13 para carros AI4 (HW4) e uma nova versão "v14.3 Lite" que leva estacionamento, saída de vaga e marcha à ré aos carros HW3 [1]. Donos de HW3 continuam ouvindo que o computador não rodará FSD sem supervisão, sem plano claro de troca [5]. A Tesla mira o 2º trimestre de 2027 para FSD sem supervisão em carros de clientes, começando pela inclusão desses carros na frota Robotaxi, dentro das zonas do serviço [5][6]. O AI5 está em produção experimental, mas não chegou aos carros [6].

O Robotaxi roda sem ninguém a bordo em seis regiões (Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa) e com motorista de segurança na Baía de São Francisco; Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville e San Antonio vêm a seguir [7][8]. Na Europa o produto passou a se chamar Tesla Assisted Driving; nove países o aprovaram e uma votação na UE é esperada em dezembro [6][11]. Na Califórnia, a polícia disse que um motorista afirmou que o FSD estava ativo quando o carro atropelou e matou um pedestre de 71 anos na Interstate 80 em 23 de outubro; não está claro se foi o motorista ou o software que freou e desviou [10].

de.summary:
FSD (Supervised) gibt es in den USA inzwischen nur noch im Abo: Teslas Supportseite nennt 99 Dollar im Monat und sagt, ein Kauf sei nicht möglich [2]; der Einmalkauf endete im Februar 2026 [3]. Tesla meldete zum Ende des dritten Quartals 1,74 Millionen aktive FSD-Abos, einschließlich früherer Käufe, und sagt, dass mehr als 75 % der Neuauslieferungen in Nordamerika FSD enthielten [4].

Aktuelle Software ist das Update 2026.38.5.10 vom 20. Oktober: FSD v14.3.13 für AI4-Fahrzeuge (HW4) und ein neues "v14.3 Lite", das Einparken, Ausparken und Rückwärtsfahren auf HW3-Autos bringt [1]. HW3-Besitzern wurde weiterhin gesagt, dass ihr Computer kein unbeaufsichtigtes FSD schaffen wird; einen klaren Upgrade-Plan gibt es nicht [5]. Tesla peilt das zweite Quartal 2027 für unbeaufsichtigtes FSD in Kundenautos an, zunächst indem Besitzer ihre Autos in die Robotaxi-Flotte innerhalb der Robotaxi-Zonen einbringen [5][6]. AI5 ist in der Testproduktion, aber nicht in Kundenautos [6].

Robotaxi fährt in sechs Regionen (Austin, Dallas, Houston, Miami, Orlando, Tampa) ohne Person an Bord, in der Bay Area mit Sicherheitsfahrer; Las Vegas, Phoenix, Jacksonville und San Antonio sollen folgen [7][8]. In Europa heißt das Produkt jetzt Tesla Assisted Driving; neun Länder haben es zugelassen, eine EU-weite Abstimmung wird im Dezember erwartet [6][11]. In Kalifornien sagte die Polizei, ein Fahrer habe angegeben, FSD sei aktiv gewesen, als sein Auto am 23. Oktober auf der Interstate 80 einen 71-jährigen Fußgänger tödlich erfasste; ob Fahrer oder Software bremste und auswich, ist offen [10].
